04_terrapin_legacy_seqbound.why: Injected IGNORE advances receiver seq by 1 while sender seq is unchanged; dropping one encrypted packet realigns them (OpenSSH release-9.6 description).

05_terrapin_legacy_invocation_counter.why: Plaintext injection does not move the per-key invocation counter; the drop leaves the receiver one behind.

06_terrapin_strict_full.why: PROTOCOL 1.9 (a): IGNORE during initial strict KEX terminates.

07_terrapin_strict_a_only.why: Defense (a) alone suffices for this wire edit.

08_terrapin_strict_b_only.why: Defense (b) alone: reset at NEWKEYS discards the injected offset, so the drop is a mismatch.

09_terrapin_server_only_supports.why: Strict needs both markers; neither endpoint enables it.

10_terrapin_client_only_supports.why: Same as 09 from the other side.

11_strip_forward_markers.why: KEXINIT payloads are inputs to H (RFC 4253 section 8); the altered I_S breaks host signature verification.

12_strip_reverse_markers.why: Client still saw the server marker and enforces (a); in reality H would also mismatch.

13_strict_ignore_before_kexinit.why: PROTOCOL 1.9 (a): first packet must be KEXINIT.

14_legacy_ignore_before_kexinit.why: Injection without compensating drop desynchronises the counter.

15_rekey_markers_ignored.why: PROTOCOL 1.9: markers MUST be ignored in subsequent KEXINIT.

16_reset_first_only_receiver.why: PROTOCOL 1.9 (b) requires reset at every NEWKEYS; asymmetric implementation breaks after re-exchange.

17_reset_first_only_both.why: Consistent but non-compliant: the model shows no failure, which is a limitation of a benign-only check.

18_forged_encrypted_injection.why: Attacker holds no keys; forged ciphertext fails verification.

21_drop_without_inject_legacy.why: A drop alone is detected by the sequence binding.
